items.label: FormFactor Q2 FY2026 (07-29-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CO-PACKAGED OPTICS TEST IS RUNNING AHEAD OF PLAN.

set.signal: CO-PACKAGED OPTICS TEST IS RUNNING AHEAD OF PLAN (CEO Mike Slessor). FormFactor entered 2026 expecting $10-20M of CPO revenue, a quarter ago forecast the high end of that range, and now expects to EXCEED THAT RANGE BY THE END OF Q3 and to 'significantly exceed the $20 million level for the year overall'; systems-segment revenue nearly DOUBLED sequentially to a record $48.5M ('albeit off an unusually weak first quarter'), driven by a recovery in the core engineering prober business and, more significantly, accelerating CPO growth. Two drivers: growing CPO chip volumes planned for later this year, and leadership in 'the all-important test insertion one, which ensures known good die on the photonic integrated circuit, or PIC wafer, before it's combined with the electrical integrated circuit, or EIC, to form the optical module in scale up and scale-out network switches'. The CEO believes this 'represents the very early stages of widespread adoption of silicon photonics in the broader semiconductor industry' as 'traditional copper interconnect is reaching physical limits in speed, heat, and energy consumption', backed by a decade-long lab-to-fab first-mover advantage; FormFactor's piece of the served market is about $400M by 2030. The CPO piece flows through the leading foundry, a 10% customer.

items.reason: '11% of Q2 revenue' is the analyst's number (Krish Sankar, TD Cowen); the CEO says only 'again a 10% customer'. Also restores the CEO's hedges ('albeit off an unusually weak first quarter', 'we believe') and the prober-recovery driver.
items.evidence: The CPO piece does flow through that 10% customer.

items.label: FormFactor Q2 FY2026 (07-29-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL-ONLY: TWO TARGET-MODEL MILESTONES CLEARED AT ONCE

set.signal: CALL-ONLY: TWO TARGET-MODEL MILESTONES CLEARED AT ONCE (CEO Mike Slessor) - FormFactor surpassed a $1 BILLION ANNUAL REVENUE RUN RATE and exceeded 50% GROSS MARGIN in the same quarter (Q2 revenue $258.2M vs a $235-245M outlook range; non-GAAP GM 53.3%, +430bps QoQ; non-GAAP EPS $0.82; systems segment a record $48.5M, +74% QoQ). CFO Aric McKinnis's margin decomposition: about a third of the sequential gain is DURABLE baseline cost reduction, a third volume, and the remaining third NON-RECURRING items (IEEPA tariff refunds and precious metal reclaimed from the Baldwin Park site shutdown) - 'we believe baseline non-GAAP gross margins have improved to around 51% at Q2 volumes'. Q3 outlook: revenue $270M +/- $10M, non-GAAP GM 54% +/- 150bps, the increase over the 51% baseline driven primarily by non-recurring IEEPA tariff refunds of about 300 basis points expected in Q3, with higher volume offset by less favorable DRAM mix; non-GAAP EPS $0.86 +/- $0.09. Capacity: the FARMERS BRANCH (Texas) site comes online in Q4 2026 and ramps through 2027 at a structurally lower cost; its initial target capacity, 'roughly equivalent to our California probes footprint to date', is expected by the beginning of 2028, when the CFO expects it to be ACCRETIVE to gross margin; 2026 cash capex for Farmers Branch and capacity additions $140-170M, pre-production ramp costs $25-30M (in G&A), partly offset by state and city incentives including a $24.2M Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund grant. 2030 target model (CFO, 'no significant changes in our expectations'): $1.6B revenue, 55% non-GAAP gross margin, $5 non-GAAP EPS.

items.reason: Removes the enricher's arithmetic note ('reads as ~$7.9M', computed from 300bps of $270M - stated nowhere); restores the CFO's hedge ('we believe'); 'entire California probe footprint' overstated 'our California probes footprint to date'.
items.evidence: Excluding the tiny items and mix favorability, we believe baseline non-GAAP gross margins have improved to around 51% at Q2 volumes.

items.label: FormFactor Q2 FY2026 (07-29-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL-ONLY: THE CPU/GPU/ASIC PROBE-CARD LADDER, SPELLED OUT.

set.signal: CALL-ONLY: THE CPU/GPU/ASIC PROBE-CARD LADDER (CEO Mike Slessor). Foundry & Logic grew on data-center CPU demand as 'the trend of increasing CPU compute intensity to enable agentic AI use cases is now broadly appreciated'. Three distinct vectors: (1) a long-term relationship and strong incumbent share with 'a leader in data center CPUs'; (2) an expanding relationship with 'the world leader in high-performance compute', where a strong networking position expands into that customer's GPU and CPU product lines - FormFactor is QUALIFIED and 'shipping production units for revenue here in the third quarter' (no GPU business was in Q2 results; GPU advanced MEMS probing is 'primarily our competitor's business' today); (3) qualification and multiple design wins at 'a large fabless XPU customer', where the CEO characterizes FormFactor's share as 'low single-digit market share at this point', with capacity commitments 'a little bit of a governor' on share growth until Farmers Branch comes online. HYPERSCALER CUSTOM ASICs are the next step-change: 'Looks like the next generation of something like a Google TPU is going to require an advanced MEMS probe because of the power and speed requirements it runs at' - the same transition GPUs made 'two, three, four years ago'; 'I don't think you'll see significant revenue contributions here in 2026, but certainly into 2027 as those parts ramp, we expect to be a key supplier'. Taiwan revenue grew more than 30% QoQ; the leading foundry was again a 10% customer.
set.figure: GPU probe cards qualified, production shipments in Q3; next-gen Google TPU looks set to need advanced MEMS probe (2027)

items.reason: Restores the CEO's hedges ('Looks like' on the Google TPU, 'primarily' our competitor's business, 'more than 30%'); '11%' is the analyst's number (Krish Sankar), the CEO says only 'again a 10% customer'.
items.evidence: Looks like the next generation of something like a Google TPU is going to require an advanced MEMS probe because of the power and speed requirements it runs at.

items.signal_prefix: Taiwan revenue grew MORE THAN 30% SEQUENTIALLY in Q2

set.signal: Taiwan revenue grew MORE THAN 30% SEQUENTIALLY in Q2 and 'the world's leading foundry was again a 10% customer' (CEO Mike Slessor) - FormFactor's probe cards and systems serving the intersection of high-performance compute and advanced packaging, where 'most of the manufacturing activity... is occurring in Taiwan'. 'The CPO piece does flow through that 10% customer', while there was no GPU business in Q2 results for it. To support 'the exceptionally steep ramps of complex devices like GPUs and custom ASICs', FormFactor expanded its multi-year partnership with Keystone Microtech (Zhubei, Taiwan) for local assembly and service capability.
set.value: 10% customer in Q2; Taiwan revenue grew more than 30% QoQ

items.reason: '11% of revenue' is the analyst's number (Krish Sankar, TD Cowen: 'TSMC being 11% customer'); management says only 'a 10% customer'. Taiwan growth was 'more than 30%'.
items.evidence: Second quarter revenue from Taiwan grew sequentially by more than 30%, and the world's leading foundry was again a 10% customer.

items.signal_prefix: CALL-ONLY / THE DDR SNAP-BACK, SEEN FROM THE PROBE-CARD SIDE

set.signal: CALL-ONLY / THE DDR SNAP-BACK, SEEN FROM THE PROBE-CARD SIDE (CEO Mike Slessor): Q3 DRAM revenue is forecast COMPARABLE to the record Q2 'but with a significant underlying shift from HBM to DDR'. The reason is the memory shortage itself - 'As you've heard recently from all our major DRAM customers, the supply environment continues to be extremely constrained, and our customers are shifting their wafer start mix to DDR designs to capture the profit opportunity provided by significant DDR price increases'. Because probe cards are specific to each customer chip design, 'we expect DRAM mix to track these dynamic customer product shifts while these unusual end market conditions persist'.

items.reason: The 'near-real-time proxy for where DRAM makers are pointing capacity' line was the enricher's interpretation, not management's; replaced with the CEO's own sentence.
items.evidence: Since probe cards are specific to each customer chip design, we expect DRAM mix to track these dynamic customer product shifts while these unusual end market conditions persist.

items.signal_prefix: CALL-ONLY: HBM IS NOW ~TWO-THIRDS OF FORMFACTOR'S DRAM REVENUE

set.signal: CALL-ONLY: HBM IS NOW ~TWO-THIRDS OF FORMFACTOR'S DRAM REVENUE (CEO Mike Slessor), on 'two customers' continued adoption' of the differentiated SmartMatrix FULL-WAFER CONTACTOR in high-speed HBM4 - it lets customers 'test hundreds of completed HBM stacks simultaneously at the 10 gigabit-plus I/O data rate of HBM4'. Stacked die test insertions 'ensure a known good HBM stack before it's combined with costly GPUs or custom ASICs' in advanced packaging processes - TSMC's CoWoS and Intel's EMIB are both named. Competitive split: FormFactor's strong share is at the high-speed final stack test at two major HBM manufacturers, while there is 'lots of competition' in the core die insertions, which are a lot like regular DRAM wafer sort; FormFactor is partnering with all three HBM makers ('although our share is stronger at two of them right now') as speeds and stack heights rise from HBM4 to 4E to HBM5.

items.reason: 'Per-pin' was added by the enricher (the CEO says '10 gigabit-plus I/O data rate'); attribution and the CEO's hedge on share at the third maker restored.
items.evidence: enabling our customers to test hundreds of completed HBM stacks simultaneously at the 10 gigabit-plus I/O data rate of HBM4.
